entries.title: P0162: exact Boolean Fourier entropy–influence conjecture
entries.statement: CONJECTURE, not a proved theorem. There is an absolute constant C such that for every n and Boolean f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} under the uniform product measure, H(f)<=C I(f). Here hat f(S)=E_x[f(x) product_{i in S}x_i], H(f)=sum_{S subset [n]} hat f(S)^2 log_2(1/hat f(S)^2) with zero terms set to zero, and I(f)=sum_{S subset [n]} |S| hat f(S)^2. The Boolean-valued hypothesis is essential. The dated 2026-09-07 local label attempted_un is historical; current global openness was not exhaustively certified by this source check.
assumptions: one constant independent of n and f
base-2 logarithm; a different fixed base only rescales C
entries.domain: probability theory; analysis of Boolean functions

source.revision: as-read-2026-10-10; exact form corroborated by O'Donnell-Wright-Zhou, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~odonnell/papers/fei.pdf, Introduction

relations.rationale: The existing attempt shows why dropping Boolean realizability from this exact conjecture invalidates an entropy-versus-mean-cardinality route; it neither refutes nor proves P0162.
